questions.question: What is the safest default disposition when a record has an unknown license or broken provenance?
options: Publish it because the text looks useful
Quarantine it with a reason code until policy resolves the uncertainty
Delete the source metadata and continue
Assign the average license of the rest of the corpus
questions.explanation: Unknown eligibility is not evidence of permission. Quarantine preserves the record and decision context without silently publishing it.

questions.question: In a deterministic early-exit cascade, why can gate order change CPU work without changing the final retained set?
options: Every record eventually passes all gates
A record rejected by any gate remains rejected, but an earlier failure avoids later calls
Later gates automatically become less accurate
The order changes every gate threshold
questions.explanation: When gate predicates are fixed, the union of failed records stays the same. Cheap, high-rejection gates can stop doomed records before expensive evaluation.

questions.question: A quality threshold rejects 18 of 60 human-eligible records. What is the false-rejection rate?
questions.explanation: False-rejection rate is false rejections divided by all human-eligible records: 18 / 60 = 0.30, or 30%.

questions.question: Why must threshold audits report important slices separately?
options: A corpus-wide average can hide concentrated false rejection or leakage
Every slice must use a different model architecture
Slice metrics guarantee causal fairness
Small slices never require human review
questions.explanation: Aggregate rates can look acceptable while one language, source type, or population bears most errors. Slice results expose that distribution.

questions.question: Which release artifact best supports auditing and reprocessing after a policy change?
options: Only the retained document count
A mutable dashboard without dataset identity
An immutable manifest linking source snapshot, policy version, model hashes, reason counts, and slice audits
The name of the engineer who ran the job
questions.explanation: A release must bind data identity to the exact policy and evidence used. That lineage makes decisions reproducible and reviewable.

questions.question: A pass rate drops after the source mix changes. What should the operator do first?
options: Lower every threshold immediately
Compare versioned source and slice distributions, then sample the changed decision reasons
Delete quarantined records
Assume the classifier degraded
questions.explanation: Pass-rate movement is a symptom, not a diagnosis. Source-mix, policy, schema, and model changes must be separated before thresholds are changed.
